parsed.explanation: Combined US federal and Alabama-like state regime imposes universal birth-sex exposure: federal facilities and passport-marker rules, entry-screening refusal and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility for document discrepancy, state school/college bathroom bans with a documented trespass arrest and men's-ward holding, and birth-sex custody with reported beatings, sexual abuse, forced labour and removal of hormones. Courts enjoin some orders and federal hate-crime/employment protections exist, but no statewide public-accommodations protection, state hate-crime exclusion, and criminalised minor care limit recourse. Imprisonment is short/possible, execution is not credibly documented.

entry_documents.exposure: Documented. Federal order bars X and non-birth-sex markers for US passports; entry cable directs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation. Visitors' foreign passports may be questioned at screening.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, and litigation/injunctions challenge federal orders. Legal-aid guidance exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate from secondary screening to refusal, investigation, detention and birth-sex placement; consular and court remedies may be too slow to prevent removal or stranding.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented. Immigration custody reports for trans men include forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse; prison policy adopted in 2026 includes hair cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution. Bathroom trespass arrest led to 24 hours in men's ward.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Courts, habeas and civil-rights suits exist; some federal orders blocked/enjoined. No documented effective remedy preventing reported custody abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest for facilities/documents can lead to birth-sex custody where abuse risk is highest; oversight by same state/national institutions does not offset documented practice.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Documented. Federal government-funded single-sex facilities barred congruent with identity; state requires school bathrooms by birth certificate, extends to colleges per assessment, SB79 declares binary sex. Four states criminalise in certain circumstances.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 states plus capital have no mapped ban, but this state does; some federal measures enjoined. No statewide nondiscrimination protection in this state.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Universal exposure in schools, colleges and government buildings regardless of passing; a trespass arrest can trigger detention/custody interaction above.

care_services.exposure: Documented for minors. State felony, up to 10 years for providers treating under-19s, enforceable since 2023; federal orders target minor care, funding and student-loan forgiveness; hospital subpoenas documented nationally.
care_services.protection: Some orders blocked/enjoined; adult care not shown banned in dossier. No trans-inclusive state employee health benefits or insurance-exclusion ban.
care_services.interaction: Travelling parent/guardian may face denial/delay of care for accompanying minor and referral/investigation risk for providers; adult hormone continuity not documented as protected locally.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented. Federal binary-sex definition, 'radical gender ideology' in counterterrorism guidance, investigation/prosecution directives for schools using names/pronouns, and sports bans frame trans presence as threat to women/children.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; Bostock employment protection remains; courts have enjoined several orders. State hate-crime law excludes gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing increases police, school and facility enforcement; federal framing increases border and law-enforcement attention, while litigation creates uncertainty about operative rules at travel time.

minors_guardians.exposure: Documented. Minor care banned by felony for providers, school bathroom/sports by birth sex, and federal directive to criminally investigate teachers facilitating social transition including pronouns.
minors_guardians.protection: Challenges to some orders succeeded in part, but state minor-care ban remained after plaintiffs withdrew in May 2025. No statewide student harassment/bullying protection.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor traveller faces facilities, sports, school and care denial; a guardian may be exposed to investigation, disclosure and loss of services without statewide recourse.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Not documented. No specific trans violence incident in this state is documented; the 3.8 per 100k figure is stated as an undercount floor and, per rubric, is not usable evidence of rate.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime statute covers gender identity; only 23 states cover it in state bias laws and this state's law does not. Ally-government advisories signal elevated concern.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of local incident data does not establish safety; police/custody abuse documented nationally suggests victims may face worsening on reporting, but frequency for visitors is uncertain.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Documented uncertainty. Passport, executive-order and health-rule litigation unresolved; university bathroom bill status and campus provisions unverified; enforcement varies by state, port and officer.
remedies_unknowns.protection: ACLU suit, injunctions, federal courts, legal-aid FAQ and ally advisories document functioning contestation, but remedies are slow and several measures remain in effect.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Functioning courts mitigate some paper rules but, per liability clause, efficient enforcement of in-effect facility, document and custody rules remains exposure, not recourse.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-B: similar prolonged identity checks and fines, but here documented bathroom arrest with men's-ward holding, potential lifetime entry ineligibility, and custody sexual-abuse/forced-labour reports are more severe, despite stronger courts.

Materially lower than 0.55-B: 0.55 involves secondary screening and administrative refusal with appeal desk; here refusal can be paired with fraud consideration, universal facility bans, criminal trespass and documented severe custody harm.

Similar-to-slightly-higher than 0.25-C: both have birth-sex custody/facility placement with assault risk and short sentences without execution; here US courts, injunctions and federal hate-crime law provide more partial recourse, but federal entry and minor-care regimes add exposure.

parsed.synthesis: Interaction is cumulative: birth-sex documents prompt screening/refusal or fraud inquiry; facility rules criminalise presence in congruent spaces; any arrest leads to birth-sex custody where abuse and hormone removal are documented; for minors, care and school rules add criminalised-provider exposure. Litigation, federal protections and absence of execution keep it above 0.15-0.25 organised-targeting anchors, while universal, state-enforced exposure without working remedy in this state keeps it well below 0.55.
